analysis: The only change is in .github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py, WorkflowBoundaryTests (head lines 731-737). It replaces the assertions that the workflow gates retarget (edited) events with assertions for an opt-in label workflow. The new assertions are: types: [labeled]; a run-threat-model label gate on pull_request_target; label removal via an API call with failures ignored; no blacksmith runners; and runs-on: ubuntu-24.04. The concurrency-placement assertions are unchanged. This is test-only code with no runtime behavior in the provider, coordinator, or cache paths, so no canonical threat IDs such as TB-002, TB-003, TB-011 or T-041 are affected. The relevant security property is CI-side: a secret-bearing pull_request_target workflow that must not check out PR head code. The unchanged test at head lines 738-776 still asserts that boundary: no head.sha or head.ref, persist-credentials false, scanner checkout not from base.sha, and pinned dependencies. The workflow YAML (.github/workflows/threat-model-review.yml) is not supplied in this batch, so I could not verify that it matches the new assertions. The labeled trigger limits runs to users who can apply labels, which narrows exposure. One unverified question for integration: the 'labeled' type fires on any label addition, and the job-level if gate should check label.name; the test asserts that gate string exists. The label-removal step's '|| true' makes failures silent. Neither is evidenced as a regression here. No findings.
